items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: Jimmy Hartwell and Jimmy Lord on clarinet always did it.

ctx.x: Well, I'm sure that it arose from a number of experiments, and some of these features do seem... Oh, my God. All right. Thank you, Mary. Goodbye. Goodbye. I'm sure that... You were talking about dynamics before...

Well, I was talking about the Wolverines and the effect that they had on the Austin boys, as far as a conscious feeling on tempo. And the breaks, which were important things at that stage of the game, were used that way. The rule in the Wolverines used to be that any break you took had to not only sustain the rhythm but improve it. And the result was, if you go back and play those Wolverine records with that idea in mind, you'll understand that's exactly what all of them were doing. Bob Gillette, the guitar…
Well, I thought about that the Indiana school took liberties with rhythm, which I don't particularly remember the Chicago boys using. But they exchanged favors on such elements, did they?
